key_idea: A valid tower is a chain under 'fits inside with rotation', so the order is forced except among identical blocks; only the orientation of each block needs a 2-state DP.
sketch: Normalize each block to (min,max) and sort descending. Identical blocks can be permuted freely, contributing a product of group-size factorials. Run a DP over the sorted list with state = orientation of the current block (squares have a single orientation since both give the same footprint); a transition to the next block in orientation (w,h) inside (W,H) is allowed iff w<=W and h<=H and contributes (W-w+1)(H-h+1) lattice positions. The first block sits at (0,0) with 1 or 2 orientations. If the blocks do not form a chain the DP naturally becomes 0. O(n log n); reduce the 1e9-sized factors mod p before multiplying. Stress-tested against a permutation brute force.
